scenes.tts: Twelve years. That is what insulin cost Frederick Sanger — fifty-one amino acids, read one stubborn position at a time, when nobody knew whether reading them would even mean anything.
scenes.narration: Twelve years. That is what insulin cost Frederick Sanger — fifty-one amino acids, read one stubborn position at a time, when nobody knew whether reading them would even mean anything.

scenes.tts: In 1943 the field knew a protein was a chain of amino acids and knew the twenty-odd letters of the alphabet. What nobody knew was whether the letters spelled a word, or whether each protein was a different random draw. Sanger settled it.
scenes.visual: 1943: chain, alphabet; word vs random; settled
scenes.narration: In 1943 the field knew a protein was a chain of amino acids and knew the twenty-odd letters of the alphabet. What nobody knew was whether the letters spelled a word, or whether each protein was a different random draw. Sanger settled it.

scenes.tts: When the sequence finally surfaced he wrote that proteins are definite chemical substances possessing a unique structure in which each position in the chain is occupied by one and only one amino acid residue — a single sentence that killed both the periodic-pattern theory and the random-mixture theory at once.
scenes.visual: definite substances; one residue per position; two theories killed

scenes.tts: He did not trust a result he could check only one way: because, as he put it, the methods used were new and were qualitative rather than quantitative, he gathered far more overlapping fragments than the bare logic required, cross-checking every conclusion from several directions before he would believe it.
scenes.visual: one check not enough; overlapping fragments; cross-check

scenes.tts: He was, by his own cheerful admission, academically not brilliant. He scrubbed hospital floors as a conscientious objector during the war and declined a knighthood because he did not want to be different. When the great genome center at Hinxton asked to take his name, he made one condition: it had better be good.
